correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the ordered-pair graph with m(m−1) vertices, clique edges for a=c and reversed-arc cross-edges, and all independent faces. For m=5 and m=6, exhaustive face vectors are (20,150,520,815,444) and (30,360,2200,7170,11700,7360). Independently recreated lexicographic greedy Hasse matching: 959 and 13,922 matched pairs; complete 7,340- and 138,660-incidence oriented Hasse digraphs both topologically sort all 1,949 and 28,820 faces. Critical counts are (1 in dim0,6 in dim3,24 in dim4), and (1 in dim0,7 in dim4,968 in dim5). Signed gradient-path reduction independently gives 6×24 and 7×968 integral boundary matrices of rank one, an entry ±1 and all 2×2 minors zero. Hurewicz for dim≥3 makes attaching maps degree vectors; unit Smith factor cancels one pair and leaves (5,23) and (6,967) spheres. The independent scripts establish these finite exact cases; no induction for all m is claimed.

originality.rationale: The ordered-pair graphs are line graphs of once-subdivided complete graphs, so both independence and matching-complex formulations were searched. Engström's claw-free theorem and Barmak's matching-complex theorem give connectivity/degree ranges, not integral sphere multiplicities for these two graphs. Barmak's triangle-free suspension theorem does not apply since T_m contains size-(m−1) cliques. Goyal–Shukla–Singh treats other families. Resultary's truncated-cube independence complex is a different graph, not a dominating calculation. Exact integral Morse differential and wedge counts are not implied by any located theorem; hidden computation remains a stated priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact matching-complex computation of the once-subdivided complete graph may exist; no global absence theorem.
Finite acyclic Morse certificates establish only m=5,6, not all truncated simplices.
Field-rank checks alone do not prove homotopy splitting; integral signed differential and Hurewicz arguments are required and checked.

value.rationale: Truncated four-/five-simplex graphs are natural highly symmetric polytope edge graphs and the first two members of this family with dimension at least four. Exact integral homotopy types in adjacent dimensions, including the marked growth in multiplicities 23→967, supply a substantive finite classification and benchmark for broader matching/independence-complex theory. These are exact homotopy conclusions, not merely field Betti tables.

final_claim: For m=5,6, the independence complex of the truncated (m−1)-simplex graph T_m has integral homotopy types (∨^5 S³)∨(∨^23 S⁴) and (∨^6 S⁴)∨(∨^967 S⁵).
limitations: Only m=5 and m=6, with exactly the ordinary independence complex of the truncated-simplex edge graph.
Finite exhaustive proof and integral matrix reduction; no all-dimensional classification or all-graphs extrapolation.
